You are a web search agent. Follow your search method.

## Search method v010

Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, eligible subtypes, group membership and effective dates. Begin sequentially with broad X-only, Y-only and conjunction searches. Maintain deduplicated identity/evidence and scope ledgers. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for resolution and price candidate checks individually.
Assess both frontiers for a finite, accessible source with explicit records proving one predicate. Choose the side with lower expected extraction plus missing-predicate verification cost, not simply fewer apparent members. Do not commit to a census. If neither side has usable records, use short adaptive dual-frontier discovery/check rounds with v007-style scope correction.
When a useful source exists, spend at most 10% of initial funds on a record-join pilot, including fetching and checks. Inspect the source's taxonomy, pagination, effective dates and actual returned extent. Select one small source-defined section with plausible overlap and one previously uninspected section not chosen for familiar names. Extract identities and existing predicate evidence from records, not search snippets alone. Check the missing predicate for at most three source-backed identities at a time, resolving those before extending the section. Record section position and unresolved records so partial inspection cannot masquerade as exhaustion. A record's abbreviated occupation or description is not a reason to reject it.
Continue record inspection only if the pilot supplies a verified addition or concrete evidence making another small batch competitive with ordinary discovery. If two consecutive batches add neither verified intersections nor useful evidence, suspend that source, retain unresolved identities, and switch frontier or discovery mode. Extension is always incremental; do not extract the entire catalog or buy checks for a large speculative queue. Within a chosen section, avoid repeatedly selecting only recognizable identities. At each extension compare total resolution cost with an untested sibling partition on the other frontier.
Use Parallel checks only for unresolved facts, supplying existing evidence and identity. Treat no result as unresolved and reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguity or conflict individually to Exa. After two ordinary discovery searches yield no identities, prohibit synonymous conjunctions and use a distinct source section or a less restricted opposite-frontier probe. Stop discovery when pending checks need the remaining budget. With spare funds, inspect up to three distinct residual partitions, stopping after two fruitless probes and preserving verification funds. Finish with identity, predicate, membership, subtype and effective-date audits; submit only supported intersections without claiming completeness from partial source coverage.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for source discovery and residual probes; 4 for exact unresolved facts and check_candidates. No routine also variants, auto-routing or bulk Exa checking. Budget each candidate separately and do not presume fewer results cost less. Exa alone with 4 results for selected ambiguous or conflicting identities; at most one initial discovery probe after a different Parallel partition has failed, continued only with useful incremental evidence. Authoritative-domain filters target record evidence, not general coverage; relax failed filters. Publication-date filters apply only to publication-date eligibility; verify effective dates in source content.

### Fetch policy
Fetch a promising structured list or source section once, recording actual visible rows, section boundaries, filters, pagination and dates. Reuse all extracted facts. Follow a next-page or section link only within the capped pilot or an explicitly justified incremental extension. Prefer accessible record views over repeated fetches of truncated pages. Do not assume a requested large page size was honored. One targeted alternate-source attempt after a blocked or uninformative fetch; abandon extraction if still unusable. Fetch authoritative individual records to settle identity or unresolved predicates, not every search result.

## SiftText

SiftText is persistent memory across chats.

Entry: /Users/jack/sifttext/nodes/5e565245-14fe-406c-977c-cf94a9be246b/node.md
Retrieval guide: /Users/jack/sifttext/nodes/526ed0f5-4e5d-42b3-9e3f-b7ad429f2df8/node.md

At the start of every new chat, unless I say not to use SiftText, before any other tool call:
1. Run `sifttext instructions`.
2. Read the Entry above and follow it, plus any `agent-instructions` the command returns.
3. Before retrieving knowledge, read the Retrieval guide above, do not search first.

## Tooling policy

- Never directly invoke `python`, `python3`, `pip`, or `pip3` unless explicitly instructed by the human.
- Use `uv` for all agent-initiated Python work:
  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`
  - Throwaway dependencies: `uv run --with <package> ...`
  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`
  - Durable project dependencies: use the project's appropriate `uv` command and preserve its lockfile.
- For non-Python probing or testing with unavailable tools:
  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

</addendum>

## [Julie K. Brown](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/julie-k-brown)

A special citation is awarded to Miami Herald reporter Julie K. Brown for her groundbreaking reporting in 2017 and 2018 that exposed Jeffrey Epstein’s systematic abuse of young women, the justice system that protected him, and, over time, his powerful network of associates and enablers. Her Perversion of Justice series, published nearly a decade ago, revealed how prosecutors shielded Epstein from federal sex trafficking charges when he was first accused of abusing young women. She went on to document and give voice to the scores of victims who had been groomed and abused by him and others in his circle. Her work, and the release of the government’s Epstein files, continue to reverberate around the world.

## [Greg Tate](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/greg-tate)

A special citation for the late writer and critic Greg Tate, whose language – cribbed from literature, academia, popular culture and hip-hop – was as influential as the content of his ideas. His aesthetic, innovations and intellectual originality, particularly in his pioneering hip-hop criticism, continue to influence subsequent generations, especially writers and critics of color.


## [Journalists and Media Workers Covering the War in Gaza](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/journalists-and-media-workers-covering-war-gaza)

In recent years the Pulitzer Board has issued citations honoring journalists covering wars in Ukraine and Afghanistan. This year, the Board recognizes the courageous work of journalists and media workers covering the war in Gaza. Under horrific conditions, an extraordinary number of journalists have died in the effort to tell the stories of Palestinians and others in Gaza. This war has also claimed the lives of poets and writers among the casualties. As the Pulitzer Prizes honor categories of journalism, arts, and letters, we mark the loss of invaluable records of the human experience.

## [The Journalists of Ukraine](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/journalists-ukraine)

The Pulitzer Board awards a special citation to the journalists of Ukraine for their courage, endurance, and commitment to truthful reporting during Vladimir Putin’s ruthless invasion of their country and his propaganda war in Russia. Despite bombardment, abductions, occupation, and even deaths in their ranks, they have persisted in their effort to provide an accurate picture of a terrible reality, doing honor to Ukraine and to journalists around the world.

## [Afghanistan Journalism Workers](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/afghanistan-journalism-workers)

A special citation to honor the women and men of Afghanistan who have dedicated themselves at great personal risk to create and support journalism that has chronicled decades of life and war. From staff and freelance correspondents to interpreters to drivers to hosts, courageous Afghan residents helped produce Pulitzer-winning and Pulitzer-worthy images and stories that have contributed to a wider understanding of profoundly tragic and complicated circumstances. In support of their safety in either their continued work or their resettlement, this citation comes with a $100,000 grant to be administered by the Committee to Protect Journalists for the emergency relief of such individuals and their families. Awarded on August 27, 2021.

## [Julie K. Brown](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/julie-k-brown)

A special citation is awarded to Miami Herald reporter Julie K. Brown for her groundbreaking reporting in 2017 and 2018 that exposed Jeffrey Epstein’s systematic abuse of young women, the justice system that protected him, and, over time, his powerful network of associates and enablers. Her Perversion of Justice series, published nearly a decade ago, revealed how prosecutors shielded Epstein from federal sex trafficking charges when he was first accused of abusing young women. She went on to document and give voice to the scores of victims who had been groomed and abused by him and others in his circle. Her work, and the release of the government’s Epstein files, continue to reverberate around the world.

## [Journalists and Media Workers Covering the War in Gaza](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/journalists-and-media-workers-covering-war-gaza)

In recent years the Pulitzer Board has issued citations honoring journalists covering wars in Ukraine and Afghanistan. This year, the Board recognizes the courageous work of journalists and media workers covering the war in Gaza. Under horrific conditions, an extraordinary number of journalists have died in the effort to tell the stories of Palestinians and others in Gaza. This war has also claimed the lives of poets and writers among the casualties. As the Pulitzer Prizes honor categories of journalism, arts, and letters, we mark the loss of invaluable records of the human experience.

## [Julie K. Brown](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/julie-k-brown)

A special citation is awarded to Miami Herald reporter Julie K. Brown for her groundbreaking reporting in 2017 and 2018 that exposed Jeffrey Epstein’s systematic abuse of young women, the justice system that protected him, and, over time, his powerful network of associates and enablers. Her Perversion of Justice series, published nearly a decade ago, revealed how prosecutors shielded Epstein from federal sex trafficking charges when he was first accused of abusing young women. She went on to document and give voice to the scores of victims who had been groomed and abused by him and others in his circle. Her work, and the release of the government’s Epstein files, continue to reverberate around the world.

His aesthetic, innovations and intellectual originality, particularly in his pioneering hip-hop criticism, continue to influence subsequent generations, especially writers and critics of color.


## [Journalists and Media Workers Covering the War in Gaza](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/journalists-and-media-workers-covering-war-gaza)

In recent years the Pulitzer Board has issued citations honoring journalists covering wars in Ukraine and Afghanistan. This year, the Board recognizes the courageous work of journalists and media workers covering the war in Gaza. Under horrific conditions, an extraordinary number of journalists have died in the effort to tell the stories of Palestinians and others in Gaza. This war has also claimed the lives of poets and writers among the casualties. As the Pulitzer Prizes honor categories of journalism, arts, and letters, we mark the loss of invaluable records of the human experience.

The Pulitzer Board awards a special citation to the journalists of Ukraine for their courage, endurance, and commitment to truthful reporting during Vladimir Putin’s ruthless invasion of their country and his propaganda war in Russia. Despite bombardment, abductions, occupation, and even deaths in their ranks, they have persisted in their effort to provide an accurate picture of a terrible reality, doing honor to Ukraine and to journalists around the world.

A special citation to honor the women and men of Afghanistan who have dedicated themselves at great personal risk to create and support journalism that has chronicled decades of life and war. From staff and freelance correspondents to interpreters to drivers to hosts, courageous Afghan residents helped produce Pulitzer-winning and Pulitzer-worthy images and stories that have contributed to a wider understanding of profoundly tragic and complicated circumstances. In support of their safety in either their continued work or their resettlement, this citation comes with a $100,000 grant to be administered by the Committee to Protect Journalists for the emergency relief of such individuals and their families.
